content:
# 1 Enoch Chapter 90 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Dreams — Animal Apocalypse

---

**1** In the vision I watched ravens attack the lambs [Seleucid forces against the Jews] — they seized one of the lambs, dashed sheep to pieces, and devoured them.

**2** I watched until horns began growing on the lambs [the Maccabees rise up]. The ravens beat down their horns. But then a great horn sprouted on one of the sheep [Judas Maccabeus], and their eyes were opened.

**3** He looked at them and their eyes opened. He cried out to the sheep, and the rams saw him and all ran to his side.

**4** Despite all this, the eagles, vultures, ravens, and kites kept tearing and swooping down on the sheep and devouring them. The sheep stayed silent, but the rams wept and cried out.

**5** The ravens fought the great horn, trying to break it down — but they had no power over it.

**6** I watched as the shepherds [angelic powers], eagles, vultures, and kites all gathered and urged the ravens to break the horn of that ram. They all attacked it, but it fought back and cried out for help.

**7** Then the man who had written down the shepherds' records and brought the book to the Lord of the sheep [the recording angel] came down to help the ram. He showed it everything.

**8** I watched as the Lord of the sheep came to them in wrath. All who saw him fled; they all fell into his shadow before his face.

**9** All the eagles, vultures, ravens, and kites gathered together — and with them came all the wild sheep of the field. They all came together to break the great horn of the ram [all nations against Judas].

**10** I watched as the man who had written the book by the Lord's command opened it before the Lord of the sheep — revealing how those twelve last shepherds had destroyed far more than all their predecessors.

**11** Then the Lord of the sheep came to them, raised the staff of his wrath, and struck the earth. The earth split open. All the beasts and birds fell from among the sheep and were swallowed up — the earth closed over them.

**12** A great sword was given to the sheep. They went out against all the wild beasts and killed them, and all the remaining beasts and birds fled before them.

**13** I saw the man [God/the Ancient of Days] sitting on a high throne of judgment. The books of the living were opened before him. His entire host and his whole court stood before him, and everyone's heart was filled with joy because the righteous man [the faithful remnant] had been protected and recorded there.

**14** I watched as the seventy shepherds were judged, found guilty, and thrown into the fiery abyss.

**15** I saw that man [the leading apostate? the chief fallen Watcher?] thrown into an abyss — blazing with fire and pillars of flame. And the seventy shepherds were judged, found guilty, and thrown in.

**16** At the same time, another abyss opened in the middle of the earth, full of fire. The blinded sheep [apostate Israelites] were brought forward, judged, found guilty, and thrown into the abyss where they burned. This abyss was to the right of that house.

**17** I watched those sheep burn — their very bones burning.

**18** Then I stood and watched as they folded up the old house [the Second Temple, or Jerusalem itself]. They dismantled all the pillars, beams, and ornaments together with it, carried it off, and placed it in the south of the land.

**19** Then I saw the Lord of the sheep bring a new house [the New Jerusalem] — greater and loftier than the first — and set it up where the first had stood. All its pillars were new; its ornaments were new and larger than those of the old one. All the sheep were brought inside it.

**20** And I saw all the surviving sheep, and all the animals on earth, and all the birds of the sky, bow down before those sheep and do homage to them, begging and obeying them in everything.

**21** Then the three clothed in white [the archangels from ch. 87] who had taken me up before — together with the ram — took hold of me and set me down among those sheep before the judgment had taken place.

**22** All those sheep were white, and their wool was thick and clean.

**23** All who had been destroyed and scattered, and all the animals and birds, assembled in that house, and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced with tremendous joy because they were all good and had returned home.

**24** I watched as they laid the sword down — the sword that had been given to the sheep — brought it back into the house, and sealed it before the Lord. All the sheep were invited into the house, but it could not hold them all.

**25** All their eyes were opened. They all saw the good. Not one of them was without sight.

**26** And I saw that the house was enormous — vast and wide and completely full.

**27** Then I saw a white bull born with great horns [the Messiah]. All the animals and birds of the earth were afraid of him and made petition to him continually.

**28** I watched as all the generations were transformed — they all became white bulls [all of creation restored to Adamic perfection]. The first among them became a lamb [?], and that lamb became a great animal with great black horns on its head. The Lord of the sheep rejoiced over it and over all the oxen.

**29** I slept among them — and then I woke up and saw everything.

**30** This was the vision I saw while sleeping. When I awoke I blessed the Lord of righteousness and gave him glory.

**31** Then I wept — a great, uncontrollable weeping. My tears would not stop until I could bear it no longer. They flowed because of everything I had seen; for it will all come to pass, and all the deeds of all people were shown to me in their order.

**32** That same night I remembered the first dream, and I wept and was troubled because of it — because I had seen everything that was to come.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 90 is the climax and resolution of the Animal Apocalypse.*

*SYMBOLISM: ravens attacking lambs (v. 1) = Seleucid persecution of Jews under Antiochus IV Epiphanes; lambs growing horns = the Maccabees (the Hasmonean revolt, 167-160 BCE); great horn (v. 2) = Judas Maccabeus (d. 160 BCE); ravens, eagles, vultures, kites = Seleucid military forces; shepherds joining battle (v. 6) = angelic powers supporting the Seleucids; recording angel (v. 7) helps the Maccabees; Lord of the sheep in wrath (v. 8) = divine intervention; twelve last shepherds (v. 10) = the final period of angelic rule; staff of wrath smiting earth (v. 11) = the final divine judgment; books of the living (v. 13) = the heavenly ledger; seventy shepherds judged (v. 14) = the angelic rulers condemned; blinded sheep in abyss (v. 16) = apostate Jews; old house folded up (v. 18) = the old Jerusalem/Temple removed; new house (v. 19) = the New Jerusalem; white bull (v. 27) = the Messiah (the restoration of Adamic humanity — white like Adam); all becoming white bulls (v. 28) = eschatological transformation of all creation back to Adamic perfection.*

*This chapter was almost certainly written during or just after the Maccabean revolt (c. 165-160 BCE), making it one of the earliest datable apocalyptic texts. Judas Maccabeus as the 'great horn' was still alive when it was written.*
